## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-11

### Spec revision 57: `M11.C.55`'s predictor and `M11.C.48`'s matched baseline (T-001 step 2, T-185, T-206) (2026-11-10)

- **Built**, the version 2 definition plan's step 2 (`docs/implementation_plan_version_2_definition.md` §4.1): the two
  changes the owner decided 2026-11-09 and held for the next batch that moves the engine hash.
- **B1, `M11.C.55` (T-206).** The criterion now reads two directional readouts — the relief predictor against the main
  supplier over the weeks before the window (`predicted_main_supplier`) and against the run's own chance
  (`predicted_over_chance`) — and a pass needs both; birth order and the supplied count stay report-only
  (`birth_order_hits`, `parents_supplied`, learnings P2). The relief is read `relief_lead_weeks` (52, `[I]`,
  `config/bowen/criteria.md`) before the window, not at its start. The lead is a criterion setting, not a model
  constant, so no constant moved and the sweep does not reach it.
  `src/bowen/ensemble/criteria_d2.py`, `criteria.py`; `tests/bowen/test_criteria_sc.py` (three new `test_m11c55_t206_…`).
- **B2, `M11.C.48` (T-185, the owner's Q3 (a)).** The baseline reads only the uncut ties acted on by as many of their
  two members as the cut tie (`acted_across`, `sides` in `src/bowen/readouts/negative_runs.py`); T-185's probe
  (`tools/c48_carrier_probe.py`) was read rather than re-measured. A first cutoff with uncut ties in contact but none
  of its own sides is left out of both arms and counted in a fourth exit, `unsided_cutoffs` (report-only), beside
  `unmatched_cutoffs` (T-123) and `no_contact_cutoffs` (T-179); the four exits are exclusive and a `FirstCutoff` whose
  flags disagree now raises. **This also changes `M11.C.48` on the Phase B family**, whose fail is the owner's accepted
  finding of 2026-11-03; that acceptance stops applying if the verdict moves at the regeneration.
- **Engine hash** `927550dfcb8a` → `d3779684dd53`. Nothing else a run computes changed: the committed Phase C trace is
  byte-identical but for its revision stamp, and `docs/review/phase_c_famdiag_seed7.json`, re-rendered by
  `tools/famdiag_export.py`, differs in that stamp alone. **No record is regenerated here** (the plan's step 4, split across both
  Macs), so every committed record still stands on `927550dfcb8a` and the eleven record-current tests that read the
  engine hash are strict expected failures, each with that reason — revision 55's pattern for the same situation. No
  verdict is reread and no disposition is drafted (step 6, the owner's, one at a time).
- **Step 3 in the same commit** (outside `config/bowen/`, so not in the hash): `config/sweep/sweep.md` declares the
  constant sets for `M11.C.52` (seven cue constants) and `M11.C.55` (the learner's seven, ranges copied from their
  existing rows) — 85 constants, 341 rows, 36 criteria — with the set choice stated: a cue constant that acts but that
  no row credits is out of both sets (T-126's rule), and `relief_lead_weeks` is a criterion setting the sweep cannot
  reach. Checked by `tests/test_version_2_sweep.py::test_m17e1_s2_6_the_two_cue_criteria_are_declared_with_their_credited_mechanisms`.
- **Suite:** 1473 tests: 1457 pass and 16 are strict expected failures (2026-11-10, this Mac).
- **Documents:** the spec (revision 57, `M11.4`, `M11.C.48`, `M11.C.55`, both `M11.5` rows),
  `docs/model_explainer.md`, `docs/readouts_phase_c.md`, `docs/spec_revision_log.md`, `docs/REVIEWER_READING_LIST.md`,
  `docs/SPEC_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md`, `docs/theory/_STATUS.md`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the plan's status line,
  T-206's item, `config/bowen/criteria.md`, `config/sweep/sweep.md`, and the generated `docs/spec_index.jsonl`,
  `docs/spec_rules/` and `docs/spec_coverage.md`. `tests/doc_claims.json`'s suite-size history entry for T-181's
  sweep now points at the archive, which holds that entry. `config/bowen/constants_changes.md` needed no
  entry: no constant moved.
- The four oldest live entries (the full sweep on revision 47's engine, the emergence audit built, the audit's step 4,
  the audit's carriers of the 10 L0 survivors) moved to `docs/CHANGELOG_archive.md` verbatim, for
  `tests/test_doc_size.py`'s limit.
- **From the two review passes on the diff** (one `learning-qa`, one correctness), all of medium severity or higher
  fixed in the same batch: each exit that leaves a first cutoff out of `M11.C.48`'s arms now reports the mean run of
  what it left out (`left_out_mean_run`, the report-only `unmatched_left_out_run` and `unsided_left_out_run`), so a drop
  that selects on the run itself is visible and not only counted (P2/P9); `tools/c48_carrier_probe.py`'s check held its
  rows against the pre-T-185 baseline and exited on real seeds, and now holds the readout's own baseline
  (`tests/test_c48_carrier_probe.py`, new); `tools/t176_negative_run_trace.py` counts unsided cutoffs apart from
  unmatched ones, and `tools/sc_pass_probe.py`'s call to `supplier_run` was broken by B1's new argument and is now
  checked against the criterion's own declaration (`tests/test_sc_pass_probe.py`); `tools/group_g_readout.py` reads the
  two new columns. `M11.C.55`'s two compared readouts are not read to the same week — the supply is counted over

- `tests/bowen/test_render.py` carries no revision-57 mark: it reads a revision string, not the engine hash, and its two
  artifacts are regenerated here, so a mark would have turned the suite red by passing.
- **Mutation proofs** (2026-11-10, measured; the tree restored after each): twelve mutants over the fifteen tests this
  batch wrote, each test turned red by at least one — the lead dropped, prior supply counted over the whole run, chance
  dropped from the compared readouts, chance not read as the share over the children, `sides` fixed at 2, the baseline
  no longer matched on sides, the left-out means fixed at 0, the exit guard removed, the unsided cutoff counted as

  mutation note says so.
- **The strict expected failures go 5 → 16, and all eleven new marks sit on tests that already existed.** Every one is a
  record-currency test that fails at the cache lookup, before any criterion is evaluated, because the cache holds no
  entry for `d3779684dd53`: the five in `tests/bowen/test_ensemble_record.py`, the three in
  `tests/bowen/test_phase_d_record.py`, `test_m111d_phase_d_mutation_record_is_current`,
  `test_lx25_committed_pilot_replays_fixed` and `test_lx16_report_is_current`. No test written in this batch is marked,
  and no criterion's verdict is reread here.

### T-207 closed: the LLM experiment's replay reads behavior, not the engine hash (2026-11-09)

- **Decided by the owner, 2026-11-09:** "Replay by behavior (Recommended)", relayed by another Claude session.
- **What.** `experiments/llm_agents/summary.py::replay_differs` decides whether a replay is the committed run: the
  committed summary must carry the hash of its own content, the replayed summary without `engine_hash` and
  `summary_hash` must equal it, and the replayed choices must equal `choices.jsonl.gz` where it exists. `replay_all`
  (`runner.py`) refuses a run on any difference, naming the recorded hashes that moved; on a match it restamps
  `summary.json` with the engine it was replayed on and leaves `run.json`, whose engine hash is the live run's
  (provenance). Tests first: `test_lx8_t207_replay_reads_behavior_not_the_engine_hash` (a moved engine with the same
  behavior is restamped; a moved engine whose acts differ, every prompt the same, is `not_replayable`) and
  `test_lx8_t207_replay_refuses_changed_choices_or_a_summary_off_its_hash`; with the behavior check removed the first
  and `test_lx8_replay_that_differs_is_not_replayable` (now changing a behavior field under a consistent hash) fail. From the learning-qa pass: a replay that ends in another status than the committed run's, or a `complete` run
  with no committed summary, is refused too (`test_lx8_t207_replay_refuses_a_changed_status_or_a_complete_run_without_its_summary`,
  red with the status check removed), and a replay with no committed choices to compare logs that the summary decides.
- **The runs.** `runner replay` replayed all 31 complete runs from their cached responses, with no live call and no
  spend: every one `complete`, every `summary.json` restamped from `0b363cb3186c` to `927550dfcb8a`, and only those two
  fields moved; no run record, cached response or choices file changed. The three strict expected failures
  (`test_lx25_committed_pilot_replays_fixed`, `test_lx10_run_record_fields`, `test_lx16_report_is_current`) are
  removed; LX.10 now checks the record's engine hash against the current engine, not a literal.
- No edit under `src/bowen/` or `config/bowen/`; the engine hash did not move (`927550dfcb8a` before and after).
- **Documents.** `docs/plan_v3_llm_agent_experiment.md` (status line, §8's replay, LX.8's row),
  `experiments/llm_agents/README.md`, the report's method text (`experiments/llm_agents/config/report_text.md`) and the
  regenerated `docs/llm_agent_experiment_report.md`, T-207's record, `TODO.md` and its archive, `CLAUDE.md`'s suite
  count (1486 tests: 1481 pass, 5 strict expected failures), `docs/REVIEWER_READING_LIST.md`, the generated
  `docs/spec_coverage.md`. The spec has no LX criterion, so it is unchanged. To keep this file under
  its size limit the entries "Spec revision 47: `M11.C.48` reads both arms under one contact condition" and "T-179: the owner's
  decision on `M11.C.48`'s readout, and the plan" moved verbatim to `docs/CHANGELOG_archive.md`.

### Version 3, part 2: the LLM-agent experiment built, plan steps 1–6 (T-183) (2026-11-06)

- **What.** `docs/plan_v3_llm_agent_experiment.md` §11 steps 1–6, under `experiments/llm_agents/` (its README): the
  config loaders and five config files; the arms A0–A4 with each seed's tokens and A3's derangement; the pure prompt
  renderer and the banned-term lint; `LLMSource`, the engine `Source` that has each living family member choose its
  week's outcome from the policy's legal set through a chooser while the external agent stays on the policy; the
  client (cache first, one retry loop, the parse and one re-ask; the SDK imported lazily, its own retries off, pinned
  `anthropic==2.6.0`); the gzipped per-run response cache; the budget's estimate and per-round worst case; the run
  record of §8; the summary, the report and the command line. Tests under `tests/experiments/llm_agents/`, 75, each
  named for its LX ID; no test calls the API. The A0 baseline (no call, no cost) was run for its five seeds and is
  committed with the generated report, `docs/llm_agent_experiment_report.md`.
- **Reviews (step 6).** One learning-qa pass, one correctness pass and a security review of the client layer (no
  finding at confidence 8 or above). Fixed in the same batch, each with a test: replay skipped runs that never
  finished instead of relabelling them `not_replayable` (P1), and now compares the replayed summary with the committed
  one, so a change that leaves every prompt the same is caught; spend is summed from the response caches, so a run that
  crashed before its record still counts (P6); a fully cached round is not charged against the cap, and the estimate
  is checked against the total cap as well; the Models check goes through the retry loop (P5); a `retry-after` longer
  than the backoff cap is honoured up to `retry_after_max_seconds`; the runs not started are written to
  `runs/phase-<name>.json` (P2); the change after an act in the history is measured to the person's next round; the
  worst case counts the output schema; key-shaped test strings are built at run time; the root `.gitignore`'s `runs/`
  is anchored to the root, so the experiment's runs are tracked. Left for the owner: A4 removes the tension line and
  the history's changes, but the tie strain and believed pair tension lines, which move after the agent's own acts,
  still show (§2's intent against LX.7's wording).
- **Beyond the plan, named at build.** Two more config files, `prompt_text.md` and `report_text.md`, so that no prompt
  or report wording is in code; the status `stopped_permanent`; the A0 arm includes the standard spells, as the
  ensemble's assembly does (LX.17). The plan's §5, §6, §7, §8 and §12 say so.

### Spec revision 54: `M11.5`'s note for `M11.C.42` names the relieved receiver (T-199) (2026-11-06)

- **What.** `M11.5`'s note for `M11.C.42` said reuse is read with `M4.C.1d`'s contact "returned to a relieved
  seeker". `M4.C.1d` returns part of a delivered contact to its sender when the delivery relieves its receiver, so the
  note now says the contact is returned to its sender by a relieved receiver, as T-171's version 2 note does. Spec
  revision 54, wording in `M11` only; no rule, class, verdict or status changed. `docs/SPEC_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md`'s
